chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihrān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān and ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam together, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, who said:

Written tablets came out to us from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام while he was in prison: “My covenant is to the eldest of my sons, that he should do such-and-such and do such-and-such; and as for so-and-so, do not let him attain anything until I meet you, or Allah decrees death upon me.”

key_terms.أَبِي الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam referred to in this report
key_terms.أَكْبَرِ وُلْدِي: the eldest of my sons, indicating the designated recipient
key_terms.أَلْوَاحٌ: written tablets or parchments conveying the Imam’s message
key_terms.الْحَبْسِ: imprisonment, the condition in which the Imam issued the writing
key_terms.لَا تُنِلْهُ شَيْئًا: do not let him attain anything, a restriction concerning a named individual
key_terms.يَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ عَلَيَّ الْمَوْتَ: Allah decrees death upon me, referring to divine decree over death

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā’s عليه السلام directive to his eldest son during imprisonment?
ai.summary: This report relates a written directive issued by Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام while he was imprisoned. It indicates designation, instruction, and restricted access regarding authority and affairs, making it significant in discussions of the Imam’s succession and administration.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mihran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Sinan and Ali Bin Al Hakam, altogether from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar who said,

‘The tablets (written parchments) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> came out to us, and he<sup>asws</sup> was in the prison: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> Covenant it to the eldest of my<sup>asws</sup> sons, that he<sup>asws</sup> should do such and he<sup>asws</sup> should do such, and so and so will not attain anything until I<sup>asws</sup> meet up with you, or Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Ordains the death upon me<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ahmad ibn Mihran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Ali ibn al-Hakam all from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar who has said the following.

“Certain tablets came out to us from abu al-Hassan (a.s.), when he was in jail, that said, “My instructions and directives to my eldest son to do so and so. As far so and so is concerned, do not give him anything until I will meet you or Allah will decree otherwise.”
